rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing late eluters. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

The first method already achieves the maximum CRF. Shorten the gradient while holding composition endpoints and temperature fixed to seek a faster fully resolved method, using the substantial resolution margin.

Reduce the gradient by one grid step to seek a shorter fully resolved method. The minimum resolution of 2.46 at six minutes provides margin, although the first pair is approaching the limiting region.

Keep the shortest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature one step to test whether elution can be accelerated without losing the first pair's narrow resolution margin. Injection 3 remains a maximum-score fallback.

Test a two-minute gradient with a narrower solvent window and lower temperature to preserve the critical early-pair separation. Heating reduced that pair's resolution; cooling and a less aggressive endpoint may enable a faster maximum-score method.

Raise the endpoint one step to accelerate the late peak during the final hold. This tests whether the early pair retains R ≥ 1.5 despite the slightly steeper gradient; established maximum-score methods remain available if it does not.

Return to the four-minute gradient and raise the starting organic fraction to accelerate elution. Lowering temperature to 35 C should provide additional early-pair selectivity to help preserve full resolution as the starting composition increases.

Raise the starting organic fraction relative to injection 6, reducing the gradient slope while retaining its stronger final wash. This tests whether the early pair can recover the small resolution deficit and deliver full resolution with the last peak below four minutes.

Shift both endpoints upward one grid step, preserving the slope that gave full resolution in injection 8. The stronger endpoint should accelerate the last peak; this run checks whether the earlier elution preserves the critical first-pair separation.

Shift both endpoints upward another grid step while maintaining the successful gradient slope and temperature. This should shorten late-peak retention further while testing whether the first pair remains fully resolved as it approaches the early elution region.

Continue the successful upward shift of both endpoints, reaching the maximum final organic fraction without changing slope. This should further shorten last-peak retention while checking that the early pair still meets R ≥ 1.5.

Raise only the starting organic fraction one step to accelerate elution further while reducing gradient slope. Check the early pair carefully as it approaches the column dead-time region; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Raise temperature one step with the fastest confirmed fully resolved gradient unchanged. The first pair now has some resolution margin, allowing a controlled test of faster elution while preserving the maximum CRF.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step while holding temperature fixed to test further acceleration. This probes the early-pair resolution boundary near the dead-time region, with injection 13 retained as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Back off the starting organic fraction to the last fully resolved setting and test one temperature step higher. This locates the thermal resolution boundary around the fastest confirmed maximum-score method without repeating an injection.

Test whether cooling restores the early-pair separation lost at the higher starting organic fraction in injection 14. This completes the nearby composition–temperature boundary check while retaining injection 13 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Reduce the endpoint one step from injection 13 to seek more early-pair resolution margin with only a modest increase in late-peak retention. The maximum CRF is already secured; this tests a potentially more robust, still rapid alternative.

Lower the starting organic fraction one step from injection 17 to move the first pair away from the dead-time region and test its resolution margin. This explores a nearby rapid alternative while retaining injection 13 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Cool injection 17 by one step to strengthen the critical early-pair separation while keeping a rapid two-minute gradient. This seeks a larger resolution margin at maximum CRF; injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Lower the endpoint one more step to test whether a shallower gradient adds useful early-pair resolution margin while retaining rapid elution. The maximum score is already secured, and injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test the remaining immediate lower-starting-composition neighbor of injection 13, the fastest confirmed fully resolved method. This checks whether moving the early pair farther from the dead-time region preserves full resolution with the strongest endpoint and modest heating.

Cool injection 18 by one step to recover early-pair resolution margin in a rapid method whose first peaks are farther from the dead-time region. Injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method; this tests a nearby alternative with greater separation margin.

Raise temperature one step from injection 20 to shorten its late-peak retention while testing whether its improved resolution margin survives warming. Injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, with the maximum CRF already secured.

Narrow the gradient window from injection 22 to seek additional early-pair resolution margin while keeping all peaks well within ten minutes. This tests another likely maximum-score method; injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved choice.

Raise temperature one step from injection 24 to shorten retention while using its early-pair resolution margin. This final local refinement avoids repeating a method; injection 13 remains the fastest confirmed method achieving the maximum CRF of 1.000.
